coverage_notes:
SOURCE BASIS. The strongest evidence is the school's own football site (mackbrown-texasfootball.com) captured on the Wayback Machine bracketing the title game: the coaching staff directory at https://web.archive.org/web/20060110101429/http://www.mackbrown-texasfootball.com/pages/coachingstf.html (archived Jan 10, 2006 — six days AFTER the Jan 4, 2006 Rose Bowl BCS title game) and the football office contact page at https://web.archive.org/web/20051210183546/http://www.mackbrown-texasfootball.com/pages/contactus.html (archived Dec 10, 2005, in-season). I diffed the staff directory against its Dec 10, 2005 capture (20051210183200) and the two are IDENTICAL in personnel and titles, so the 15 people on that grid were on staff continuously through the championship game. No arrivals or departures mid-season were found; no midseason_note applies to anyone. WHAT IS FULLY RECOVERED. Head coach, all 9 on-field assistants, strength & conditioning head, both graduate assistants, both football-operations administrators, and the 4 named administrative assistants — 19 people, every one from a 2005/Jan-2006-dated primary source. The Jan 2005 hire announcements for Chizik, Giles, Rucker and the Feb 2005 GA announcement (Koonz, Lewis) are cited as corroboration. WHAT IS PARTIALLY RECOVERED (IMPORTANT CAVEAT). No 2005 Texas media guide survives anywhere I could reach — archive.org's Texas football media guide collection jumps from 1960 to 2006, and the school site never posted one. The last 6 rows (Arias, Boyd, Hardin, Robertson, Jean Bryant, Brian Davis) therefore come from the 2006 media guide's "Football Support Staff" section, and their 2005 presence is established by explicit tenure statements whose arithmetic covers the 2005 season (e.g. Boyd "begins his fourth season" in 2006 = 2003-06; Arias "19th year" in 2006; Robertson "14th season"; Hardin "10th season"; Jean Bryant "ninth year"; Brian Davis "ninth year at Texas"). These are inference-by-tenure from a 2006 publication, NOT a 2005-dated roster — treat them as a lower confidence tier than rows 1-19. Note also that Robertson (equipment) and Hardin (sports medicine) are department-wide roles attached to football, not football-exclusive positions. TIERS I COULD NOT RECOVER AT ALL. 1. ANALYSTS AND QUALITY CONTROL: zero rows. Texas in 2005 had no publicly documented analyst or QC tier; the NCAA off-field-analyst role had not yet proliferated, and neither the staff directory nor the 2006 guide lists any such position. I found no evidence such staff existed, as opposed to merely being undocumented. 2. ASSISTANT STRENGTH COACHES: Jeff Madden's assistants are completely undocumented. The 2005 site lists only Madden; the 2006 guide's S&C spread is heavily OCR-garbled and names no assistant strength staff. Texas certainly had assistant strength coaches; I could not name any with a source, and I did not guess. 3. STUDENT ASSISTANTS / INTERNS / VIDEO ASSISTANTS: none documented beyond Arias. 4. ADDITIONAL SUPPORT NAMES SEEN BUT DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED: the 2006 guide also shows Charlie Craven (supervisor of physical rehabilitation) and team physicians Dr. Mark Chassay, Dr. Andrea Pana and Dr. Carey Windler. I excluded all four because their entries carry NO tenure statement, so nothing ties them to the 2005 season rather than 2006 alone. They are real people on a real page — they simply fail the season-attribution test, and I would rather under-report than assert an unsupported ring. EXCLUSION CHECKED AND CONFIRMED. Major Applewhite has a staff bio still live on the 2005 site (pages/staff/applewhite_bio.html), which could mislead: that page is a stale 2004 artifact reading "Second season at Texas," and he is absent from both the Dec 2005 and Jan 2006 staff grids — he left for Syracuse with Greg Robinson after 2004. He is NOT 2005 staff and is excluded. Similarly excluded as departed-before-2005: Greg Robinson, Dick Tomey, Mike Haywood (each named as the person replaced in the Jan 2005 hire releases). WIKIPEDIA. The 2005 team-season article carries only an infobox (Brown, Davis, Chizik, Akina) and no coaching staff section, so it contributed nothing beyond the top four; its infobox role labels are split across HTML lines and are not quotable as contiguous strings, so Wikipedia quotes come from article prose instead. QUOTE RELIABILITY. Every quote in this dataset was mechanically verified as an exact substring of a fresh fetch of its exact cited URL — 36/36 passed, checked against both raw HTML and tag-stripped text. Where a staff-grid role is quoted without the name attached (Kennedy, Madden), it is because the source separates name and title with a
tag; the quoted role string is the verbatim contiguous text run sitting directly beneath that person's name and photo in the grid, and each of those two people carries a second corroborating source.
